brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two-tier unit: three full bases at level 0 (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) with full covers on the three level-1 bases (cover:-1,0,1;full;top, cover:0,0,1;full;top, cover:1,0,1;full;top) forming a 453 mm-wide top deck, dressed with a standing row of books (prop:1) across it so the book-shelf purpose is visible from front and top.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the half base piece:0,1,0;half-n and drawer:0#-1,2#cut on the half base piece:-1,2,0;half-n, both at the front of the ground tier, tidied over with half-n top covers.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only and knows nothing about materials, strength or load ratings; the parts are 3D printed in a user-chosen material. So no 50 kg rating can be certified or claimed from this build, however sturdy the shape. The unit was made as one connected body (all level-0 cells in a single group) with capOpenFaces caps and lockJoints joint bolts applied, but that is not a load guarantee.

finish.summary: Built a two-tier Hex Cluster shelf: three full hex bases at ground level stepped up to three covered full bases above, giving a wide flat top deck now holding a standing row of books (plus one connected body and bolted joints from the house rules). The two front ground-tier cells are half bases carrying exactly the two drawers asked for. Check is clean and the mesh gate is clear. The 50 kg book-load rating is left unmet honestly: fit is all the configurator verifies, and load capacity depends on the user's print material and settings, so no rating can be promised — I would not shelve a guaranteed 50 kg on printed plastic on the strength of this model.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building a book shelf with two drawers — the 50 kg rating I can't certify (the configurator checks fit only, not strength), but I'll build the unit and flag that. First, looking at what exists and where drawers fit.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
